accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS K.G.6 (compose simple shapes to form larger shapes, the two-triangles-with-full-sides-touching example) and 1.G.2, the NCTM and Clements and Sarama learning trajectory for shape composition, and standard pattern block relations: 6 equilateral triangles, 3 rhombuses or 2 trapezoids fill the hexagon, and a square cannot tile it because 90 degree corners do not match 120 degree ones. Each composite was verified geometrically: two congruent right triangles along the hypotenuse make the rectangle; two squares make a 2 by 1 rectangle; two right isosceles triangles along a leg make a larger isosceles triangle; four squares make a 2 by 2 square. UK trapezium is noted beside trapezoid.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early composition errors (Clements and Sarama, Learning and Teaching Early Math; Sarama and Clements 2009 composition trajectory): orientation changes a shape's identity (challenge turned and pointup, p5, the turn step), two squares make a bigger square (step 2 prediction, p1, challenge bigsq), shapes touching at a vertex or with a gap count as joined (step 5 feedback, p3, challenge corner and gap), there is only one way to fill a shape (step 3 prediction, m5, challenge oneway) and any block fits (the square block, m3, challenge squares).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcompose is about putting shapes together: rotating congruent triangles in quarter turns until they fill a rectangle, animated joins of squares and triangles that must then be named, a pattern-block hexagon filled wedge by wedge with ways tracked, a house built by dragging shapes into matching spaces, and a snap test between a gap, a corner and a full side. flagshape counts sides and corners, flagfit is a shape sorter, flagtiles is area by unit squares; none composes new shapes. Gate similarity under 30% to every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover each idea by doing it: an untouched triangle on its side is refused by the rectangle until turned, the joined squares are outlined as one shape before naming and a bigger square answer is refused with the long and short side reason, the square block is refused by the hexagon with the corner reason, a second fill that repeats the first is not counted, and a corner or gap snap is refused until a full side touches. Done messages restate the idea.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: 'No, a rectangle is not made of triangles' (two triangles fill it), 'A bigger square' for two squares (the joined outline is 2 by 1), and 'No, only one way works' for the hexagon (the task needs two different fills).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with twelve distinct wrong-answer messages: bigger square, triangle with 4 sides, circle from triangles, triangles cannot join, 3 or 4 triangles in a hexagon, corner touching, a gap, only one way, only squares, a turned triangle as a new shape and a triangle only when pointing up. The same why() messages give feedback inside the naming step.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 2.8 and adult at 7.8 (family limits 5.0 and 10.0). Kid sentences are short and concrete (Two triangles can make a rectangle; A turned triangle is still a triangle). Canvas labels are short: 'Tap to turn', 'What shape is it now?', 'Ways found: 1 of 2', 'Shape 1 of 4: a square'. The adult text names compose, side, vertex, rotate and the shape names.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: triangles make a rectangle, squares make a rectangle or bigger square, full sides must touch, turning and many ways. Items spread across naming composites (p1, m1, m2, m6), full sides (p3), turning (p5, m8), hexagon filling (p4, m3, m5) and counting pieces (p2, m4, m7) with no repeated stems.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android screenshots in light and dark for every step at the start, during Show me and at the end: the rectangle and both tray triangles fit in all four turns after narrowing the pieces and moving them in from the edges, the three name choices stack in a column at 360 px so none overlap, the hexagon and four block tiles fit with readable names, the house and the shape card sit side by side, and both pieces in the touch step stay inside the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Turn triangle and Put triangle in for each piece, Join and the three names, Add a block for each of the four blocks, one button per house space for the current shape, and Leave a gap, Touch at a corner and Touch along a full side. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with what happened and why. walk.cjs runs every task with Show me and axe WCAG 2.1 AA in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
